title: Spectator mesh: sampled shadow gatekeeper & tenant cost failsafes
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Summary:
We need a lightweight, low-risk mechanism to run 'spectator' copies of production requests against candidate model variants for telemetry, quality checks, and A/B comparison without increasing tenant spend unpredictably. This ticket implements a Spectator Mesh: a sidecar-level gatekeeper that duplicates requests to spectator backends under an adaptive sampling policy, enforces per-tenant cost caps, and provides enriched telemetry (latency, token counts, divergence scores).

Goals:
- Safe duplication: no request path latency regression; non-blocking spectator invocation.
- Adaptive sampling: system-wide and per-tenant sampling that adjusts with budget and model load.
- Tenant isolation: ensure a tenant cannot exceed a configured shadow budget; enable automatic spectator suspend for a tenant that reaches its quota.
- Cost controls: global and per-tenant token/cost accounting with circuit-breakers and gradual throttling.
- Observability & audit: per-request duplicate trace IDs, token accounting, replayability markers, and dashboards for cost and quality regression.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not change inference kernels or model quantization. It focuses on routing, sampling, accounting, and safety.

Constraints and design decisions considered:
- Duplication must be asynchronous and memory-bounded; we use a bounded LIFO queue per worker to reduce tail memory pressure.
- Avoid replicating large request bodies across services; use short-lived reference handles when running in Dedicated clusters with shared storage.
- Sampling decisions should be deterministic for a given request ID and tenant when possible to support reproducible A/B analysis.

Risks:
- Under-accounting of tokens due to response streaming; mitigations include conservative estimators and adding post-hoc reconciliation via billing records.
- Tenant blowouts if sampling config is misapplied; mitigations include default low sampling rates and enforced max cost caps per tenant.
acceptance_criteria: Spectator duplication path is non-blocking and adds <1ms p50 latency to production RPCs under nominal load
Adaptive sampler adjusts sample-rate in response to configured budget depletion and load signals
Per-tenant shadow budget enforced: when budget is exhausted, spectator duplication for that tenant is suspended and a signal is emitted to the control-plane
End-to-end telemetry is emitted: duplicate_trace_id, original_token_estimate, spectator_token_usage, divergence_score
Playbook and runbook for emergency suspend/resume of spectator traffic documented and tested
technical_notes: Spectator Gatekeeper lives in the request ingress path as a lightweight module (C++) with a configurable async worker pool
Sampling policy hierarchy: tenant_override -> route_policy -> global_adaptive_policy. Deterministic sampling uses HMAC(request_id, tenant_id, seed) % 10000 < rate*10000
Cost accounting: use token_estimate = max(estimated_request_tokens, conservative_upper_bound_from_model_profile) until reconciled with actual billing
Queue strategy: bounded per-worker LIFO with drop-oldest backpressure to avoid head-of-line blocking
Persistence: for Dedicated/VPC deployments allow zero-copy handles; hosted deployments send a compact reference and replay token to the spectator runtime
Auto-fallback: if spectator backend returns errors > 5% over rolling window, auto-throttle spectator requests globally for that target model variant
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag behind 'spectator_mesh' per-environment. 2) Canary enablement: enable for internal tenants only at 0.1% sample rate. 3) Gradually ramp to 1% and then 5% for internal tenants while monitoring cost delta & divergence metrics. 4) Enable per-specified external customer cohorts (opt-in) with strict per-tenant budgets. 5) After 2 weeks of stable metrics, flip default to low-rate for broader internal monitoring. Each ramp step gated by automated checks and human approval.
test_plan: Unit tests for deterministic sampling function and quota accounting
Load tests to verify <1ms median added latency and bounded memory under X RPS
Chaos scenario: simulate spectator backend failures and validate auto-throttle and circuit-breaker behavior
Billing reconciliation test: generate synthetic streams and verify token estimates vs final billing adjustments within 10% error
End-to-end integration with console dashboards and alerts (latency, spectator_cost_pct, suspended_tenants)
metrics: spectator.divergence.alert_rate (% of sampled requests exceeding threshold)
updates: 2025-01-16: Kickoff sync — aligned on scope. Team: infra, runtime, billing. Action: infra to provide tracing hooks; billing to expose per-tenant provisional counters.
2025-01-22: Prototype merged for deterministic sampler; basic unit tests added. Observed non-blocking behavior in local load test.
2025-01-29: Implemented per-tenant quota token ledger and suspension signal to control-plane (PR 1893). Deployed to internal staging cluster for functional validation.
2025-02-05: Load test results: p50 added latency 0.7ms, p95 4.2ms at 1000 RPS with 5 worker threads. Memory spike under pathological burst — changed queue to LIFO and retested.
2025-02-10: Integrated spectator metrics into console. Created canary checklist and playbook. Ready to start internal canary (0.1%).
